title: Opening: the preacher arms himself for battle against heretics
english: Again, as a soldier under orders, I take up the battle against the heretics, with Stephen, the general of piety, commanding the ranks. For just as Joshua routed the enemy while Moses prayed, so I too, with the martyr as my ally, subdue the enemies of the truth. I say this not because I trust in an abundance of words, but because I have confidence in the martyr's prayer; and so it is with confidence that I lay hold of these words. For I do not fear their bombast in speech. I do not fear the outworks of their evil-crafted deception. I have learned not to fear a fear where there was no fear. They say that Christ fears death and is afraid of it, but we, for Christ's sake, choose to die as many times as the days we live in the flesh, so that with bare head we may lead the truth in triumph. Therefore, as one who already holds the winning vote, I advance against them. For Christ encourages me through the prophet, saying: "Son of man, do not be afraid of their faces, for they will rage against you on every side. For you dwell in the midst of scorpions" (Ezekiel 2:6). I am not afraid of stinging scorpions. For I do not walk with bare feet; I have the sandals of the gospel of peace, so that even if I am bitten, I am not harmed. "And having shod your feet," he says, "with the readiness of the gospel of peace" (Ephesians 6:15). Come then, with the sandals of peace let us trample the many-formed head of the heretics, so that by the fearlessness with which we advance against them, we may teach them how greatly they err when they attach fear and timidity to the nature of the only-begotten. For those who think and speak everything without judgment and without reason, and who do not understand "Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass," vote fear against Christ and say that he is needy and lesser because he prays to the Father and seeks release from the necessity pressing upon him. Since, then, they slander the Word of God to insult God, and to reject the Spirit they chant the letter around, mocking and ridiculing the plan of salvation of Christ, and with cleverness of phrase and fluency of words they cover over their venomous bites, robbing the more innocent of their salvation—come, as those unskilled in words, let us call upon the very Word of God, so that he himself, becoming the interpreter of his own words, may expose their folly and strengthen our understanding. Tell us the meaning of what has been said, Master; unfold the leaf of the letter and show the fruit of the Spirit, so that we may not attend to the letter and die, but may run to the Spirit and enjoy life. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life (2 Corinthians 3:6). Teach us as infants, and discipline the heretics as fools; for you are the instructor of fools and the teacher of infants. To us as infants, bare the breast of grace and offer the nipple of the Spirit. Pour out the pure milk of the gospel teaching. And make the folly of the heretics plain. For if they were not fools, they would not have woven a doctrine of blasphemy to destroy your divinity. For the fool has said in his heart, it says, "There is no God" (Psalm 14:1). Strip bare their mask of impiety, so that the drama of their hypocrisy may be exposed. Show that they carry your name around for this reason: to cover over the blasphemy of their own choice. Tell us, then, Master, for what reason you came to the passion and yet decline to suffer, and why you fear the threat of the Jews—you who command us not to fear those who kill the body (Matthew 10:28). And if you fear death at all, why do you not decline death? For if it lies within your power to suffer or not to suffer, you say in vain, "If it is possible, let it pass." For in you—
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Amphilochius, bishop of Iconium, opens his homily against heretics by presenting himself as a soldier under the martyr Stephen's protection, then turns to Christ and asks him to interpret his own words in the Garden.
